name: Bikeability Perception of Street Views (Singapore, Tokyo)
description:
Method replication: same seven perception items and 0–10 scale as the paper; the images are not the paper's stimuli (new Google Street View views of Singapore and Tokyo, © Google). Ito & Biljecki (2021, Transportation Research Part C 132:103371) built a bikeability index of 34 indicators in five categories (connectivity, environment, infrastructure, perception, vehicle–cyclist interaction) for Singapore and Tokyo from street view imagery, OpenStreetMap and other data. For the perception category they ran an Amazon Mechanical Turk survey: 400 randomly selected Google Street View images per city, each rated by at least eight participants from 0 to 10 on attractiveness for cycling, spaciousness, cleanliness, building design attractiveness, safety as a cyclist, beauty and attractiveness for living. Outliers were removed with the median absolute deviation, and LightGBM models on image features predicted the ratings for all street points.

What participants do: after consent, 20 street views drawn at random from 81 (Singapore 39, Tokyo 42); for each they move seven sliders from 0 to 10. Then an attention check and how often they cycle.

Analysis as in the paper: per-image median of each item after removing ratings with MAD-based outlier scores above 3; then models predicting the scores from image features (semantic segmentation, object detection, scene classes, colour).

Differences from the original study: (1) the images are 81 new Google Street View views (2016–2026) from random points in central Singapore and Tokyo, not the paper's 800; (2) slider end labels (0 and 10 only) and the cycling-frequency question are not from the paper. The earlier version of this template pointed to a gated Hugging Face dataset with no bundled images.
